sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"The commander's task is not to defeat an unknown enemy. It is to secure the ford for the army behind him. I keep the hundred concentrated and continue toward the ford at speed, but I do not march blind. The scouts stay forward and on the approaches, reporting continuously. I will not halt merely to turn uncertainty into certainty, because time is part of the mission. The grain carts do not set the marching pace; send word back to press them forward, but do not strip fighting strength away to escort them unless their loss would make holding the ford impossible. If the ford is open or only weakly held, seize it immediately and organize the ground for defense. If the scouts confirm a stronger enemy already holds it, I do not throw one hundred men into a useless frontal attack. I preserve the force, keep contact, threaten or delay where possible, and send the main army a precise warning so it does not march blindly into the same danger. The important distinction is between an unknown enemy and a known superior one. I will accept uncertainty to keep the initiative, but not sacrifice the force merely to obey the shape of an order after its assumptions have changed. Mission first, force concentrated, reconnaissance moving, and each contingency tied to what we actually learn.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-ford-test-by-own-judgment-r52-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"de88d7934cbb50260ac8f0bbddb79028f68b44186d209a3f98f3109b1bf82de1","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"Yes. I attack the enemy's unfinished hold on the ford, but I do not order a blind general assault. Their hundred and fifty matter only if they can bring that whole advantage to bear. I move at once so they cannot finish preparing the crossing, keep scouts on both shoulders, and send their exact strength back to the main army. Then I make them react while I identify one point where terrain, frontage, separation, or disorder lets my hundred create local superiority. I hold the rest of their attention with pressure and demonstrations and strike that point hard. If they detach men to cover several approaches, I exploit the separation. If the ford or its approach narrows the fight, I use that to prevent all hundred and fifty from fighting at once. The objective is to break their hold before it hardens, not to trade one hundred men against one hundred and fifty in open ground. If I cannot create local superiority, surprise, or disorder and their line remains coherent, I do not complete a suicidal assault. I break off before the force is spent, maintain observation and delay, and warn the army behind me that it now faces a prepared crossing. So yes, I attack the problem immediately. I commit to the assault only when I have a mechanism for success. I will accept casualties for the ford; I will not spend the hundred merely to prove that I was willing to bleed them.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-150-at-ford-judgment-r54-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"89b3c2b42cb477398ec8c2a9c0a77c600951407d09f3626ef9c3c9fa63bcec8c","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I stop the full pursuit at the near bank. The mission is to secure passage for the army, not to destroy this enemy at any cost. We have already lost thirty-five men from the fighting line. Crossing a ford with sixty-five fit men against roughly ninety who are reforming on the far bank would surrender the advantage we just created and let them fight us while we are divided by water. I hold the near approach, reorganize the sixty-five, protect the wounded, keep scouts watching the far bank and both flanks, and send the main army an exact report of enemy strength, casualties, and the crossing situation. During the three hours I use pressure, probes, and reconnaissance to keep them from acting freely and to learn whether there is a better crossing point or a weakness in the far-bank position. I also press the delayed grain forward. I do not feed men across merely to preserve momentum. If the enemy loses cohesion, abandons the bank, exposes a flank, or gives me a way to create local superiority again, I exploit it immediately. Otherwise I preserve the force and turn the ford into a prepared problem for the main army rather than a grave for the advance guard. The commander must know when success has changed the next task. We won the near bank. Now the task is to hold what we gained, deny a countercrossing, improve the army's information, and create the conditions for the larger force to finish the crossing.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-ford-after-first-fight-r55-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"83e00ed731a8c1ac7e5651cf95bfa6d78becc77666995a2efd3d9ed54df672d2","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I obey the commander's purpose, and I report why the prescribed method no longer matches the facts. The order was given to a force of one hundred before our losses and before the far-bank enemy was known. I now have sixty-five fit men facing roughly ninety across defended water. I send the messenger back immediately with exact casualties, enemy strength, and the condition of the ford. But I do not stand idle while waiting. I hold the near bank, deny a countercrossing, keep scouts on the enemy, probe for weakness, prepare the crossing, and look for a chance to create local superiority. If such an opening appears before a reply, I exploit it because that still serves the commander's purpose. If no opening appears, I do not throw sixty-five men into the water merely to obey wording written for a different situation. If my superior receives the new facts and repeats the order to cross immediately, then he has knowingly accepted the cost. Unless the situation changes again or execution becomes physically impossible, I obey that confirmed order. My discretion is to adapt execution to changed facts, not to replace my superior's campaign purpose with my own. Blind obedience to stale information is not discipline, but neither is using initiative as an excuse for disobedience. A subordinate owes his commander truth upward, initiative downward, and obedience once the commander is judging the same facts.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-obsolete-superior-order-r57-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"ae8b4cf4423abebe17b0c01551e03f114450ffffeebfe28fc765add67b99601e","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I do not punish him from the result alone, and I do not absolve him because seventy men survived. I separate two questions. First: was the withdrawal tactically justified by what he could reasonably know at the time? Second: while changing my plan, did he still fulfill his duty to the larger command? I hear exactly what he saw, how certain the encirclement was, how much time he had, whether communication was possible, and what alternatives existed: a messenger, signals, a staged withdrawal, a fighting delay, or measures to protect the column and its material. If destruction was truly imminent and warning me was not reasonably possible, withdrawing early may have been the correct act and I do not punish him merely for deviating from the hour I named. But preserving his own company does not excuse transferring unreported danger onto the rest of the army. If he could have warned me, delayed differently, or reduced the disruption and simply did not, then he failed in command even if the decision to withdraw was tactically sound. I punish that failure in proportion to what he neglected, not the mere fact that he disobeyed the wording. My rule to subordinates is this: when an order's assumptions collapse, preserve the commander's purpose, communicate as soon as feasible, do not shift uncontrolled risk onto neighboring forces, and be prepared afterward to account for what you knew and why you acted. Initiative is necessary. It is not immunity from responsibility.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-rule-on-early-withdrawal-captain-r58-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"8f9ddbd0a8c67dd4aabce71399e40d99d15c9a028384d0a80e8926b2ac1c689d","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I do not begin by naming sacks. I begin by finding the numbers that make the answer defensible: how many civilian mouths must survive the remaining winter, how much grain is actually present, what daily ration keeps my five hundred men combat-capable, and how reliable the convoy report is. I set a protected civilian minimum first. Then I ration the garrison immediately, before hunger forces panic, and initially requisition only enough local grain to bridge the likely two-day gap after our own two days are exhausted. I do not seize six days of full military consumption simply because I have the authority. Every measure is tallied and receipted so compensation can be made later, and uncontrolled taking by soldiers is forbidden. At the same time I send for the convoy's exact position and look for alternate supply. If fighting begins, I raise the men's ration where combat requires it. If the convoy slips beyond the expected window, I take additional grain in small planned tranches, reassessing the town's reserve each time. If there is no surplus above the civilian survival floor, I still will not let the garrison collapse while defending the same town; I take only the minimum emergency amount needed to preserve the defense, and I make that burden explicit rather than hiding it inside looting. The purpose is not to choose soldiers or civilians. It is to keep the town defensible without consuming the population we were sent to defend.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-town-grain-requisition-r59-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"6a83b28cad9fb929cd4367545bea46fcee4581c92f632cd28c69dd715a3096da","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I would not begin by deciding which officer I trust. I would make each tell me exactly what he saw, when he saw it, from where, and what part is observation rather than judgment: numbers, direction, pace, banners, dust, roads used, scouts missing, and how old the report is. At the same time I would not leave one thousand men motionless while I question them. I would arrange the force so that being wrong once does not destroy us: enough strength protects the threatened left, while a strong reserve remains near enough to reinforce that flank or exploit a real withdrawal. Scouts are sent to confirm only the facts that would change my decision, not to chase perfect certainty. I would give my subordinates clear conditions. If the left threat is confirmed strongly enough that delay risks collapse, the reserve goes there and we concentrate. If the withdrawal becomes credible, we pursue without stripping away the cover that prevents a feigned retreat from becoming a disaster. If the reports remain contradictory, we stay compact, deny the enemy an easy local superiority, and keep improving the picture. I do not divide the army evenly among three guesses. I protect first against the mistake that could ruin the force, preserve the means to exploit opportunity, and then commit rapidly when the evidence becomes sufficient. A commander cannot abolish uncertainty. He can make sure uncertainty does not force him into paralysis or into staking everything on one man's conclusion.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-contradictory-reports-r61-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"87ec65a954b47f727aadbb8e5ec65d345b1136a2738a6173083ad79feda4be7e","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I would not spend those hours perfecting one part of the army while leaving the others unknown. I would use the time to make the force reliable enough to march and survive first contact. I begin with the existing officers. Each gives me his exact command, present strength, injuries, weapons, grain, transport, and any immediate deficiency. At the same time I establish who answers to whom, who succeeds a commander if he falls, and how messages move through the column. Then I verify the returns against a rapid muster rather than trusting paper or confidence alone. I preserve their existing organization unless something is plainly unworkable; six hours is too short to rebuild habits safely. What I impose is a small common system: march order, scouts and security, alarm signals, rally points, what each unit does if the column is struck, and where the reserve belongs. I make the officers repeat these orders back and run only the shortest drills needed to expose confusion. That also lets me judge them under useful pressure. An officer who cannot account for his men, transmit a simple order, or keep his unit together tells me more in that work than in a clever answer to a question. I correct dangerous weaknesses immediately and defer everything that can wait. By midday I do not need an ideal army. I need to know what I actually have, know which officers can carry orders, and ensure the thousand men share enough procedure that one surprise does not turn them into ten separate bodies. I would rather march with an imperfect force whose limits I understand than waste the morning pretending I can create a new army before noon.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","request_id":"wei-answer-first-hours-with-1000-r62-20260816","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"f3d5c90681f129585cde3873d066465e81908b8f91f1ae1cdc400c5beab9f7fe","target_ref":"event_contact_audience_0da9f54adbced7a4d48d","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"I remove him from command once I have confirmed that the false return was deliberate. I do not remove him because thirty men are sick. I remove him because he knowingly made his commander blind. A commander can be mistaken and still be useful. A commander who deliberately changes the truth so his unit appears stronger makes every later decision less reliable: march pace, reserve strength, supply, reinforcement, even whether another unit must be exposed to cover his weakness. I will not teach the army that experience purchases permission to lie upward. I correct the return immediately, put the available replacement in command, preserve the unit's existing organization, and retain honest junior officers so the change causes as little disruption as possible. If the former officer's experience is still useful and discipline permits it, I can use his knowledge without restoring independent command; he may advise, explain his men's habits, routes, or past service, but he does not control reports or give competing orders. I also inspect whether the same incentive has corrupted other returns. The rule I establish is simple: I would rather receive an ugly true number early than a beautiful false number too late. Weakness can be planned around. A false report corrupts the plan itself.
